title: Beware the two-faced
takeaway: Watch out for hypocrites. They're more dangerous than any snake.
scene: The poet looks at the villages and cities around him and sees fakeness everywhere. People pretend to be something they're not.

original: پنڈ وی ریا فریب دے نیں شہر جاپدے
بتے کدورتاں دے بھرے قہر جاپدے
transliteration: Pind vi riyaa fareb de nain shehar jaapde
Butte kadooraataan de bhare qehar jaapde
translation: Even the villages now seem like cities of show and deceit;
people seem like idols filled with grudges and rage.
couplets.story: Villages used to be simple and honest. Now even they feel like big cities full of fakeness and lies. People seem full of grudges and anger.

original: آب حیات لبھیا جنہاں دے واسطے
اوہ وی میری حیات لئی زہر جاپدے
transliteration: Oh vi meri hayaat layi zehar jaapde
translation: The very people I found the water of life for
now seem like poison to my life.
couplets.story: He went looking for the 'water of life' for certain people. He gave them everything good. Now those same people seem like poison to him.

original: آخر اوہناں نوں کالیاں راتاں نے گھیرنا
جیہڑے حسن جمال دی دو پہر جاپدے
transliteration: Aakhir ohnaan nu kaaliyaan raataan ne gherna
Jehre husn jamaal di do-pehar jaapde
translation: In the end, dark nights will surround them too,
those who seem like the noonday sun of beauty.
couplets.story: People who look stunning, like the midday sun, will one day be surrounded by dark nights too. Beauty doesn't last.

original: جو لوک بے اصول تے بے ضمیر نیں
ڈبدے ہوئے اوہ حسد دے وچ بحر جاپدے
transliteration: Jo lok be-usool te be-zameer nain
Dubde hoe oh hasad de vich behr jaapde
translation: People without principles and without a conscience
seem to be drowning in an ocean of jealousy.
couplets.story: People with no principles and no conscience look like they're drowning in a sea of jealousy.

original: سبق عشق دے پڑھ گئے جیہڑے سی سرفروش
عاشق سراں دی منگ دے نیں خیر جاپدے
transliteration: Sabaq ishq de parh gaye jehre si sarfarosh
Aashiq siraan di mang de nain khair jaapde
translation: Those willing to give their heads learned the lessons of love;
lovers seem to beg for heads as their alms.
couplets.story: Only the people brave enough to give up everything really learned what love is. Real lovers ask for nothing less than everything.

original: احمدؔ بچو منافقاں توں شیش ناگ نیں
انج تے وفا خلوص دی نیں نہر جاپدے
transliteration: Ahmad bacho munaafiqaan ton, Shesh-naag nain
Inj te vafa khuloos di nain nehar jaapde
translation: Ahmad, beware of hypocrites: they're giant serpents,
even though they look like a stream of loyalty and sincerity.
couplets.story: He ends with a warning. Watch out for two-faced people, Ahmad. On the outside they look like a flowing river of loyalty and kindness. Inside, they're as dangerous as a giant poisonous snake.

deeper: Hypocrisy (nifaq) is one of the faults Islam warns against most strongly; the Qur'an gives a whole chapter to the hypocrites. The poet's warning fits that teaching. 'Those willing to give their heads learned love's lessons' is the Sufi ideal again: love means total sacrifice, not words.
why: It's a short, sharp warning about fake friends, and the image of a 'stream of loyalty' that is really a snake is memorable.
prompt: How can you tell the difference between someone who is truly loyal and someone who only seems loyal?
